corpus: Mandatory recycling under the City Recycling Law, Local Law 19 of 1989 (Admin Code §§16-301 et seq.), implemented through 16 RCNY Chapter 1 (Collection); organics source separation under DSNY's Source Separation of Residential Organics Rules (2023) and Admin Code §16-308.1 / Local Law 85 of 2023, mandatory citywide from 1 Apr 2025.

rows.rule_text: Households must segregate food waste (including food scraps, fruits, vegetables, meat, dairy, grains) for organic collection and processing at DSNY-certified facilities; mandatory citywide from 1 Apr 2025.
Commercial generators must segregate food waste and ensure its separation from recyclables and trash, with penalties under Admin Code §16-308.1 for non-compliance.
Households must separate mixed paper and cardboard from garbage for recycling collection under the City Recycling Law (Local Law 19 of 1989, Admin Code §§16-301 et seq.) and 16 RCNY Chapter 1.

Commercial generators must source-separate paper and cardboard for recycling under the City Recycling Law (Local Law 19 of 1989, Admin Code §§16-301 et seq.) and 16 RCNY Chapter 1, with collection arranged through licensed carters.

Households must separate metal, glass, and rigid plastic containers plus cartons for recycling collection under the City Recycling Law (Local Law 19 of 1989, Admin Code §§16-301 et seq.) and 16 RCNY Chapter 1.

Commercial generators must source-separate metal, glass, and rigid plastics for recycling under the City Recycling Law (Local Law 19 of 1989, Admin Code §§16-301 et seq.) and 16 RCNY Chapter 1, with collection arranged through licensed carters.
Households set out residual/non-recyclable waste for landfill or energy recovery under 16 RCNY Chapter 1, following DSNY collection schedules and receptacle rules (Admin Code §16-120(a)).

Commercial generators must manage non-recyclable residual waste through DSNY-approved carters, with compliance tracked under the City Recycling Law (Local Law 19 of 1989, Admin Code §§16-301 et seq.) and 16 RCNY Chapter 1.
